item.content:encoded:
This isn't really in the article, but in my head these are paper wasps and actually do patch up the house. Sort of, as a side effect of expanding the hive into cracks and crevices like wasps do.

Eventually, the perfectly content victims are living in a pile of kindling held together by bug-spit and the power of blissful ignorance; literally swarming with "fairies" they adore. I've got an image in my head sort of like morning tea at Candyman's kitchen table.

I wonder if anything interesting happens if the homeowner is allergic to stings. Maybe just anaphylactic shock that the hallucinations cover up until death. Or maybe instead of helpful, constructive brownies the bad reaction gives visions of gremlins or other more sabotage/mischief oriented fae.

item.title: Browneys
item.content:encoded:
So I saw the title of this article was "Brownies", and I came here expecting something similar to "orgasm muffins". The first thing I saw was a picture of a bug, and I was like, "Wat?" I read a little bit, and then I realized, "Oh, like the faery - 'browney', not "brownie'."

I'm not sure how long it normally takes other people to get that…I wouldn't suggest fixing the name, though - "Brownies" is a name that draws people. That said, Browneys are supposed to love honey, not milk, I believe. I could be wrong, of course. :)

As for the rest…well, it's an explanation for an old mythical creature, and a cool bug SCP that doesn't eat you from the inside out - I like it. +1 :D

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
What are their nests made of? Wax, like with bees? "Paper", like with wasps? Something else?

SCP-779 is a species of insect similar in appearance to the common bee or a wasp.

I'm no expert on bugs, but that image looks a lot more like a beetle than a bee or wasp.

SCP-779 have been observed to operate at all times of the day, and are typically dismissed by residents as ordinary bees or wasps.

If I saw bee or wasp which was red and black I sure as heck would sit up and take notice.

When injected with the venom, victims of SCP-779 will perceive SCP-779 as small humanoid figures with wings and believe that SCP-779 are assisting with the maintenance of the residence.

Does the venom also make the victims keep the "fairies" a secret? Since otherwise these people would end up telling their neighbors, and word would get around.

As SCP-779 are voracious eaters, they will typically consume all food in the residence in a matter of days.

Insects which make nests/hives don't migrate every few days. Even if these were the exception, they'd have to have some way of carrying the eggs and grubs from one house to the next, since the queen is constantly laying eggs.
